# CLAUDE.md — working context for BetterBeltBalancer

A Factorio mod: automated belt balancers that click together into arbitrary shapes and balance items across the belts feeding and draining them (belt orientation decides input vs output). Two goals, in order:

1. **Demonstrate FkLua is fit for a serious mod** — the mod's brain is written in Go (TinyGo → wasm → Lua via [`../FkLua`](../FkLua)), not hand-written Lua.
2. **Significantly outperform belt-balancer-2**, the incumbent, which manipulates transport lines from Lua every tick.

Conventions are inherited from FkLua — read [`../FkLua/CLAUDE.md`](../FkLua/CLAUDE.md) before working here. The rules below repeat only what is load-bearing daily.

---

> **TRUNK TARGETS FACTORIO 2.1 SINCE 2026-08-24, AND ITS RULE IS ONE BELT PER BALANCER PART.** 2.1 closed the collision-mask loophole that let two interface linked belts share a part's tile, so a part carries at most one edge and a cluster that asks for more is refused. The design is [`agents/single-edge.md`](agents/single-edge.md) and the rule is `guest/go/sedge.go`; "One belt per balancer part" below is the working note. **ALL FIFTEEN SUITES ARE IN THE DEFAULT AND FOURTEEN OF THEM RUN ON EITHER ENGINE**, as of 2026-08-24: `m2`, `mar` and `upg` had their rigs REBUILT single-edge -- which is also what restored the heap-slope gate the port's first three phases shipped without -- then `mix`, `plat`, `qual`, `m3` and `edge`, and finally `mig`, which is the one suite whose rigs were deliberately NOT re-laid: its world is the INCUMBENT'S, so on 2.1 an incumbent balancer converts and is then refused, and what was added is a band laid one belt per part that converts into a working network. **AND THE RELEASE/2.0 ARM IS VERIFIED SINCE 2026-08-24 AND RECUT AT 0.2.1 ON 2026-08-26**: the whole estate is green on Factorio 2.0.77 in both `-gc` arms with `mar`'s slopes byte-identical, `mig21` and `mig` INVERT there (nothing is pruned, so a multi-edge save is adopted whole and a converted Belt Balancer save is grandfathered and RUNS at 3.997x and 2.996x one belt), and the fourteenth suite -- `flip`, which drives the setting that exists on 2.0 only -- is how the flip-off turned out to be a VETO rather than the sweep the design described, and how the veto's own spill was found and fixed. See [`agents/single-edge.md`](agents/single-edge.md), phase 9. **THE 2026-08-26 SESSION IS WHAT A 2.0 BINARY UNBLOCKS AND IT IS THE LAST OF IT**: `flip`'s observer ported (the repository's final hand-written Lua), the 2.0-flavour dump golden captured for both mod sets, and `--benchmark-verbose` re-tested and found WORKING there, which makes the 2.1.16 SIGSEGV a statement about one engine rather than about the harness.

## Critical rules

- **Rebase, never merge.** Trunk is `master`, history is linear, `git merge --ff-only` is the guard.
- **Determinism is a correctness property.** Factorio is lockstep multiplayer: no entropy, no wall clock, no iteration-order dependence in anything host-visible. Lua `pairs` order over tables keyed by anything but dense integers is a desync.
- **Documentation drift is a gate failure, not a follow-up.** Update this file in the same commit as the change it describes. When a topic outgrows this file, move it to `agents/<topic>.md` and leave an index entry here. Create `agents/` files on demand only.
- **Human-facing documents follow the house style in [`agents/docs-style.md`](agents/docs-style.md).** `README.md`, `FKLUA-GAPS.md`, the bench and test READMEs are written for a public GitHub reader: no local paths, no change-history narrative, no milestone or round codes as if known, no CLAUDE.md section citations, no agent or process attribution, and no em-dashes or en-dashes anywhere. This file and `agents/` are working notes and are exempt. Read that file before editing any of them, and run its grep check before committing.
- **Measure before believing.** Every performance claim in this repo carries the command that produced it. A variant that computes a different answer is not a faster variant — benchmarks compare outcomes (item counts delivered per output) before timings are trusted.
- **A SENTENCE THAT REACHES A DATA-STAGE PROTOTYPE'S `localised_description` MUST FIT 200 BYTES PER ELEMENT, and `make datastage-check`'s two `note` arms are what say the ones this mod can reach do.** On Factorio 2.0.77 build 84539 the engine refuses a localised-string element over 200 BYTES (not characters, and per element rather than per string) and stops the whole load, naming the offending element's 0-based index. **THE RULE IS A PROTOTYPE RULE AND NOT A WHOLE-MOD ONE**: a SETTING prototype is exempt, measured by FkRecipes at 201, 400, 1000, 2000 and 5000-byte elements all loading clean, which is why this mod's four composed setting descriptions are not chunked and are not what the note arms watch. **THIS BLOCKED 0.3.3 FROM RELEASE FROM 2026-09-14 UNTIL FkRecipes `137f4aa` ON THE SAME DAY, AND THE BLOCK IS LIFTED.** The library's own fallback sentence was 247 bytes with this mod's 39-byte setting name in it, so a typo a player typed into `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` STOPPED THE LOAD, and the `Error loading mods` dialog cannot reach the Mod Settings screen where it would be corrected; the unreleased 0.3.3 changelog and `README.md` both told a player the opposite, and neither was rewritten, because they described the release and the release was blocked. `137f4aa` chunks every literal the library composes into a PROTOTYPE's `localised_name` or `localised_description` at word boundaries into elements of at most 180 bytes, concatenation byte-identical, so that sentence comes out in TWO ELEMENTS cut at a word boundary. **MEASURED HERE ON THE SAME BINARY AT LIBRARY HEAD `61ac80c`**: that typo is exit 0 and a dump, `bbb-balancer-part.localised_description` is three elements whose concatenation is the 247-byte sentence byte for byte, and the recipe is the dropdown's own default, which is what a player who typed nothing gets. **BOTH NUMBERS IN THAT DATED ROW MOVED IN FkRecipes FIX ROUND 3 AND THE SHAPE WITH THEM**: `ca4c344` reworded the sentence to 268 bytes (229 of library constant plus this mod's 39-byte setting name), so the cut is 179 + 89 rather than 176 + 71, and `121aafc` opens the composition with the author's own `recipe-description` key in the engine's alternatives form, so the field is FOUR elements, the empty parameter and that key wrapper and the two chunks. The technology channel's note is 159 bytes and stays one piece. Measured at library head `cf66357` by `make datastage-check`'s `note-recipe` and `note-control` arms, which assert both chunk lengths and the key wrapper over what the engine put in the dump. **WHAT IS NOT MEASURED IS THE SCREEN.** The engine joins a localised string's parameters with nothing between them, so a chunk boundary SHOULD be invisible in a crafting tooltip, and nobody in either repository has hovered one: that is the client run owed since round three and it is the one thing not to take from these green rows. `test/check-datastage.py`'s `check_note_ceiling` is the standing guard, `note-recipe` and `note-control`, one per channel, each measuring every element against the ceiling over what the engine put in the dump. The whole finding is [`agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`](agents/fkrecipes-migration.md), "Fix round 2", fifth subsection, and the lift is "Fix round 2b re-adoption" after it.
- **Never test against `/opt/homebrew/bin/lua`** (it is 5.5). Factorio is doubles-only Lua 5.2.1; use `../FkLua/bin/lua52f` for host-side Lua testing.

## A committed save with a player in it

**Every "needs a player" statement this file has ever made rests on one fact, and it is a fact about how a world is MADE rather than about what a script may do.** A `game.players` entry exists only where somebody once connected. Nothing creates one: not `create_entity`, not a force, not a controller. A headless `--create` therefore has none, `game.get_player(1)` is nil in sixteen of the seventeen suites, and everything downstream of a player index -- the miner's pocket's beneficiary, the over-limit hand-back, a cursor build -- returns before it does anything.

**So the sixteenth suite starts from a save a graphical CLIENT made**, reduced to the one thing it wants out of it. `test/fixtures-player/player-2.0.77.zip` is **382,986 B**: one player, one nauvis of nine chunks, no entities, no second surface, no inventory, recorded against BASE ALONE.

**IT IS REGENERABLE FROM ANY CLIENT SAVE AND THE COMMAND IS THE RECORD.**

```sh
make player-fixture SAVE="$HOME/Library/Application Support/factorio/saves/whatever.zip"
```

`test/make-player-fixture.sh` copies the source save before anything reads it -- the user's own saves and mods directories are read-only to it -- and runs `guest/go/obs/fixplayer` over the copy TWICE. The product's file name carries the engine it was recorded on, read off `--version` rather than written down. The save this one was cut from was made by **Factorio 2.0.77 (build 84539)** with base, the three DLC mods, `better-belt-balancer` and `wormhole-belts` loaded; the source is not committed and nothing here needs it again. End to end it is about eleven seconds, and it is DETERMINISTIC: two cuts from the same source save came out byte-identical, `26c75ecb8fd47549...`, so re-cutting one to check something moves nothing.

**THE SAVE ROUTE IS `--start-server` AND `game.server_save`, BECAUSE THE OTHER ONE DOES NOT EXIST.** `--benchmark` never writes a save: `game.auto_save(name)` returns true there and produces no file and no log line, measured over 10 ticks and over 120. A server saves on demand -- and `saves/` has to exist first, or `server_save` refuses with `filesystem error: in canonical: No such file or directory`, which is how a headless server that has never saved leaves it.

**THE SECOND PASS IS WHAT MAKES THE PRODUCT COMMITTABLE.** It loads the first pass's output with base alone, so Factorio drops the prototypes and the `storage` of every mod the source save names. Measured on this one: `script.dat` **5,868,208 B -> 1,281 B**, and the whole file 3,130,691 -> 382,986. What is left is the freeplay scenario's own baked initial level (`level-init.dat`, 735,458 B uncompressed), which nothing a script can reach removes.

**AND THE CUTTER IS THE ONE PACKAGE HERE BUILT `--persist=none`, WHICH IS A CORRECTNESS MATTER.** Its schedule is keyed off the first tick it sees and the two passes run over the same world; under `packed` the second pass ADOPTS the first's heap, `start` comes back holding the first pass's tick, every step is already behind it, and the run does nothing but log its last line -- measured, pass 2 wrote no save at all. A one-shot cutter has no state worth carrying across a save, so it carries none.

**WHAT THE FIXTURE CANNOT HOLD is a connected player**, and the `curs` suite's own section is where that is measured and answered: a server load disconnects everyone and destroys their character, a disconnected player cannot be given one back, and the GOD controller -- which such a player can hold -- drives `build_from_cursor` and `mine_entity` with the same event trace, the same mine buffer and the same inventory arithmetic a character produces.

## The shipped mod holds no Lua

**Every byte of Lua in the packaged mod is generated, and `mod-data/` is graphics, locale, a changelog and a thumbnail.** The settings and data stages were ten hand-written files there until 2026-08-25 and are `guest/go/data` now — a SECOND wasm module beside the control guest, from which `fklua mod` writes `settings.lua`, `data.lua` and `data-final-fixes.lua`, one per hook the module exports.

**The old reason for the exception was wrong, and it is worth saying which half.** It read: *Factorio's data stage is declarative with no runtime and no state, so there is nothing there for a Go guest to be the brain of.* The first clause is true of the STAGE and false of this mod's use of it. That "declarative" stage branched on the engine version to decide whether two belt-connectables may share a tile, defined a runtime setting only on the versions that have one, deep-copied four base belt prototypes and patched their speed and their sprites, computed eight arrow sprites from an offset constant, derived a technology's cost from whichever tier base says it hangs off, and defined a stub entity only when no incumbent had claimed the name. None of it could be reached by `go test`, and the version branch had to be a file two Lua states each `require`d because they share nothing else.

**Two modules and not more exports on one**, which is FkLua's own D1 and is measured rather than tidy: `require` re-executes at every stage, so a control guest hooked into the data family is parsed once per stage — **+150 ms per game load** for a 3.1 MB program the stage never calls — and its package initialisers would run against a runtime API that is not there. A data module is compiled `-gc=leaking` and packaged `--persist=none` whatever the control guest's arms are, because it runs once and dies with the Lua state that built it. `fklua mod` REFUSES a data module that imports `fkapi` at all.

**One Go module, though**, and that is what paid for the pass: `guest/go/data` and the control guest share `guest/go/engine` (the version branch, which both stage hooks now call) and `guest/go/skin` (the sprite sheet's cell count, which the prototype and the runtime had each written down separately). The shared-file problem is retired rather than re-solved.

**What must not be tidied:** the `//go:noinline` marks in `guest/go/data`. Lua 5.2 keeps a jump offset in an 18-bit field, this stage is exactly the straight-line-through-small-helpers shape LLVM inlines hardest, and at `-opt=2` all six sections folded into one wasm function that lowered to a 28,139-line Lua function the parser refused (`control structure too long near 'trap_unreachable'`, measured on the first packaged build). Marked, the largest is 3,414 lines and the emitted module is 27% smaller as well. `main.go`'s header is the long form.

**The gate is `test/check-datastage.py`**, and it is a different question from `make test` — see Verification.

**`fklua mod` still `rm -rf`s its output directory** before writing, so nothing hand-written can survive there; the tree named by `[mod] data` is merged in before the directory writer AND the zip writer, so both carry the same bytes.

### What it cost, measured either side of the port

Both packages built from clean on 2026-08-25, shipped config (`--persist=packed --gc=collected`), same FkLua, same pin, same machine:

| | before | after | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `dist/better-belt-balancer_0.3.0.zip` | 453,975 B | **546,004 B** | +20.3% |
| `fk_module.lua` (the control guest) | 3,136,956 B | **3,136,956 B** | **byte-identical** |
| `fk_data_module.lua` (the data guest) | — | **1,498,245 B** | new |
| `fk_data.lua` (the shim, verbatim) | — | 24,106 B | new |
| `dist/bbbdata.wasm` | — | 141,799 B | new |
| hand-written Lua in the package | **45,037 B** | **0** | eleven files |
| members bound into the mod | 54 | **54** | of 4,859, none added |

**The control guest is byte-identical, and that is the shape of the whole change**: nothing in `guest/go` outside the new `data/` and `engine/` packages was touched, so `fk_module.lua` comes out the same file. What the zip pays is a second compiled guest for a stage that used to be 45 KB of source — 92 KB of download, once, against a data stage `go test` can reach and that cannot drift from the runtime consuming it.

**Nothing on any hot path moved, measured rather than argued.** A data module runs at load and is not in the game at all afterwards, so the standing gate is that the CONTROL guest's per-operation heap slopes do not move — and the `mar` suite's leaking arm came back **identical to the byte** against a build of the pre-port commit run in the same session: **1,280 / 352 / 1,209 / 32 / 560 / 3,736 / 2,080 B** per primitive over **3.92 MiB** of linear memory, 1,136 B of calibration at 0.0% spread, 0 items lost over 200 teardowns, 681 audits at drift=0. That is the set this file has recorded since the single-edge port, and it is what says a second guest costs the first one nothing.

**All fourteen suites are green in BOTH arms** over the ported package (1m49s collected, 1m59s leaking, one invocation each), and **no suite's numbers moved at all** — which, for a change that touches only the load-time half, is the only result available, and is the second validator behind the dump.

## Cost, research and belt speed -- the three things the data stage stopped writing down

**The mod portal's first feature request, in three parts, shipped as 0.3.1.** All three are data-stage decisions and none of them is a constant any more: what a balancer part costs to craft, which technology unlocks it and what that costs, and how fast the hidden network's belts run. **The DEFAULT of all three is what shipped before**, and that is the property everything else in this repository rests on -- every rate, every heap slope and both dump goldens were measured on it.

**The three folds live in `guest/go/tune`, which is PURE GO and is the sixth package to earn that.** The reason is `engine`'s and no other package's: **the interesting states are states of somebody else's mod set.** A fallback rung is taken only in a game with no `express-transport-belt` in it, and the speed derivation only does anything in a game with a belt faster than 0.25 -- neither is a mod set this machine can install, so inside `guest/go/data` those arms would be branches nothing could execute and nothing could check.

**SINCE ROUND TWO OF THE FkRecipes MIGRATION, TWO OF THE THREE ARE DECLARATIONS RATHER THAN CODE.** The ladders are still this package's -- `RecipePlan` is six plans and `TechLadder` is three -- and what walks them is the library's `IngredientsBy` and `CostBy`, which is the verb this mod wanted the library for. `guest/go/data/recipe.go` and `technology.go` are deleted with `item.go`, and the predicate, the type list and the two `[BBB]` fallback log lines went with them. The belt speed is unchanged and is still the data guest's own.

### The recipe, and the ladder that is the whole risk

`bbb-recipe-cost`, a STARTUP string setting, defined on both engines (unlike `bbb-multi-edge-parts`, which exists on 2.0 alone). Startup is forced rather than preferred: a recipe is a PROTOTYPE, so what it costs has to be readable at the data stage, and `fkdata.StartupSetting` is the only kind that is.

| option | ingredients |
|---|---|
| **`vanilla`** (DEFAULT) | 4 iron-plate, 2 iron-gear-wheel, 2 transport-belt -- **byte-identical to 0.3.0** |
| `cheap` | 2 iron-plate, 1 transport-belt |
| `belt-fast` | 4 iron-plate, 2 iron-gear-wheel, 2 fast-transport-belt |
| `belt-express` | 4 steel-plate, 2 iron-gear-wheel, 2 express-transport-belt |
| `splitter` | 1 splitter, 2 iron-plate |
| `splitter-express` | 1 express-splitter, 2 steel-plate |

**AND SINCE 0.3.3 A TEXT FIELD SITS BESIDE THE DROPDOWN, WHICH COST THAT TABLE NO ROW.** `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` holds a recipe the player writes in FkRecipes' ingredient language, and THE TEXT IS THE SWITCH: while it says `default` the dropdown decides, and anything else is what the balancer part is made of, with the chosen preset set aside and one line saying so. So the six values above are the whole of what `bbb-recipe-cost` allows, exactly as they were before the field arrived. It was a SEVENTH DROPDOWN VALUE, `custom`, from round three until fix round 2 withdrew it; "Fix round 2" below has why, and the short form is that Factorio resets a stored dropdown value the running release does not offer and persists the reset silently, so a seventh row was destroyed by one launch of an older release while the typed text beside it lived.

**AN INGREDIENT NAMING A PROTOTYPE NOBODY DEFINED IS A HARD LOAD FAILURE WITH THIS MOD'S NAME ON IT**, in somebody else's overhaul pack, before a prototype of theirs is read. That is the entire risk of the feature and it is measured rather than feared: with the guard removed and a plan pointing at a Space-Age-only belt, a base-only `--dump-data` dies on `Error in assignID: item with name 'turbo-transport-belt' does not exist.`

So every ingredient is a LADDER of candidate names and the first one the game actually has is what is emitted. **`tune.Resolve` walked those ladders until round two, when it was deleted, and `fkrecipes.IngredientNamed` walks them now**, through one `IngredientChoice` per allowed value; the properties are the same and where they are proved has moved:

- **No name reaches a prototype unless the game has it.** That is the library's guarantee now, asserted against a fixture World: every option in a game whose only item is `iron-plate` comes out as iron plate, and every option in a game with no ingredients at all comes out with NONE.
- **Every ladder terminates, and at the same rung**: `iron-plate`, the cheapest thing any game with belts in it has. **This is the half `guest/go/tune` still owns and it is not redundant with the one above**: the library guarantees it emits no name the game lacks, which an empty recipe satisfies vacuously, and a ladder that ends somewhere every game with belts has is what stops that being the answer. A game with no iron plate at all gets a recipe with NO ingredients, which is a strange machine and a load that COMPLETES. That is the trade, stated: never break the load, always say so in the log.
- **A rung that lands on a name the list already carries is MERGED into it, and the engine takes the result.** Every ladder ends at `iron-plate` and vanilla and cheap both name `iron-plate` at top level, so a pack that removes `transport-belt` makes the third ladder land on a name already in the list. Until FkRecipes 696387f that reached the engine as two entries and REFUSED THE LOAD -- `Duplicate item ingredients are not allowed (iron-plate exists 2 or more times).`, exit 1, no dump, no `fkrecipes:` line, on the DEFAULT preset for a player who never opened the Startup tab, which is [`agents/migration-assessment.md`](agents/migration-assessment.md)'s finding 1. The library adds the second landing into the first now and logs the arithmetic, so that player crafts a balancer part from `6 iron-plate, 2 iron-gear-wheel` and the load completes: measured on 2.0.77 behind a synthetic `bbbt-remover`, `--dump-data` exit 0, and it is `make datastage-check`'s merge arm. **The rungs are kept and the merge is what makes them legal**, which is `Item`'s substitution semantics arriving: the amount does not move down the ladder, so two belts substituted for at the same amount ARE two more plates. Dropping the terminal rung instead deletes the ingredient rather than substituting for it, prices vanilla at 8 plate-equivalent against the stock game's 11 where the merge charges 10, and fails `TestEveryLadderTerminates` six times. "Fix round 1" below.
- **The vanilla plan is byte-equal to a literal copy of 0.3.0's ingredient list**, written out a second time in the test rather than restated from the plan -- and DRIVEN THROUGH THE PLAN since round two, so the same literal is compared against a different machine.

**The predicate WAS `itemExists` here and is `fkrecipes`' `ItemExists` now**, and it probes the prototype's `name` LEAF rather than the prototype for the reason this repository measured first: `Get("item", "iron-plate")` marshals a whole prototype across the wasm boundary to answer yes or no; `name` is mandatory on everything in data.raw, so its presence and the prototype's are the same fact and the read is one string. The library reads the item family from `fkdata.DerivedTypes("item")` where this mod wrote the twenty-one types out, which is a strictly better answer to the same question: a modpack is entitled to make an ingredient a `capsule` or a `module`, and a derived list cannot be missing one.

**"The identity plan is the last resort" is the LIBRARY'S fallback now and is still a tripwire rather than a live path.** A chosen plan that resolves to nothing falls back to the DEFAULT option's plan, with a line saying so -- and no plan here can do that while vanilla resolves to something, because every ladder ends at the same rung. It exists for the plan somebody adds later.

### The technology, where the prerequisite moves with the unit

`bbb-tech-cost`, the same shape: `logistics` (DEFAULT, today's behaviour), `logistics-2`, `logistics-3`. The strings ARE the base technology names, so there is no mapping table under them. Since 0.3.3 three fields sit beside it -- `better-belt-balancer-tech-packs`, `better-belt-balancer-tech-count` and `better-belt-balancer-tech-seconds`, generated names placed by `OrderAfter` since the sync pass -- and since fix round 2 each of the three is a SWITCH OF ITS OWN, overwriting the chosen tier's unit one field at a time: a pack text on the word `default` and a number at 0 each leave that field to the tier. They were a fourth dropdown value, `custom`, from round three until fix round 2 withdrew it; "Fix round 2" below has why. The three values above are therefore the whole of what `bbb-tech-cost` allows, and a player who had stored `logistics-3` still reads `logistics-3`.

**The unit was already READ rather than written down** -- that is 0.1.0's decision and the reason this mod follows whatever an overhaul charges for a tier. What the setting picks is which technology to read, and **the PREREQUISITE comes from the same read**. Charging `logistics-3`'s science while still hanging off `logistics` would put a machine that costs blue science at a place in the tree a player reaches with red: researchable long before it is affordable, and out of order in Factoriopedia. One technology is named once and both fields come from it.

The ladder is `logistics-3` -> `logistics-2` -> `logistics` -> the vanilla fallback (20 automation science over 15 s), and a rung is taken only when that technology exists AND carries a `unit` -- the trigger-technology case 2.0 introduced and base itself uses. **The fallback emits NO prerequisite**, which is strictly better than what 0.3.0 did: `prerequisites = {"logistics"}` naming a technology nobody defined is a load error, not a cost.

**AND SINCE FIX ROUND 2 THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN KEPT, WHICH IS THE BEST FORM IT HAS HAD.** Every value `bbb-tech-cost` allows names a source technology, and that source is the prerequisite whatever the three fields beside the dropdown say, so repricing the research CANNOT move it in the tree and the cost and the place cannot come apart. There is no placement field in the plan at all: `TechSpec.CostFrom` carries the three settings and nothing else, and `TechOptions()` is the menu order and the choice table and nothing more. **WHAT THAT REPLACED, AND THE DATED RECORDS BELOW ARE ABOUT IT.** From round three until fix round 2 the dropdown carried a `custom` value that named no source, so the plan placed it by a ladder of its own -- `CustomCost.Position`, which fix round 1 made `TechOptions()` itself so that its head was `TechDefault()` by construction -- and `TestTheCustomArmTakesItsPlaceFromTheDefaultTier` and `TestThePositionLadderStepsUpAndThenLetsGo` were what held the coupling. `CustomCost.Position` no longer exists in the library, both tests are deleted, and the argument they served is discharged rather than carried: the mismatch the section above argues against, a blue-science price at a red-science place, is unreachable when every price comes with the source it was copied from. The measurements those rounds took stand as records of the shape they were taken on and are annotated where they appear.

**SINCE ROUND TWO THIS IS `fkrecipes`' `CostBy`, AND IT MOVED THREE BEHAVIOURS.** The choice, the ladder walk, the verbatim unit copy and the prerequisite moving with it are all the library's, driven by `TechLadder` unchanged. Two of the three moves are narrower and one is wider, all three are measured on the engine, and all three are graded in [`agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`](agents/fkrecipes-migration.md):

- **The fallback's science pack is probed whether or not the fallback is reachable**, so a pack with a perfectly good `logistics` and no `automation-science-pack` in it is refused at plan time (`fkrecipes: the technology bbb-balancer prices itself in automation-science-pack, which does not exist`) where the hand-rolled version loaded and copied logistics' own unit. **A load that used to succeed and now refuses**, and a migrating consumer cannot avoid it: a zero `UnitSpec` is refused for its count, so a `CostBy` always carries a fallback and a fallback is always probed. Graded **AWKWARD**, with the ask being a probe that fires only when the fallback is reached, or a pack ladder in `Pack.Name` the way `IngredientNamed` has one. **ANSWERED BY FkRecipes c7a806e, 2026-09-07, and the ask got both halves**: the `Fallback` is resolved only where it applies, so an unreachable one asks the game nothing and a game with no science pack at all loads (`TestAnUnreachedFallbacksPackIsNeverProbed`), and the pack question moved to the game that has to answer it, where a reached fallback whose one pack is absent is refused instead -- `fkrecipes: the technology bbb-balancer has no science pack the game has; research takes at least one` (`TestAReachedFallbackWithNoPackInTheGameIsRefused`). **THAT REFUSAL WAS DELETED BY FkRecipes `97a4493`, 2026-09-14, AND THE TEST RENAMED WITH IT**: it is `TestAReachedFallbackWithNoPackInTheGameIsEmittedFreeAndDisclosed`, the research is emitted with no science pack and completes for free, and the sentence quoted here exists nowhere any more. The record above is kept as it was measured; see `agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`, "Fix round 3".
- **`max_level` travels with the unit.** It lives on the TECHNOLOGY rather than in the unit, and the hand-rolled `researchUnit` read three fields of the unit and nothing else. Measured with `logistics-3` given a `max_level` of 3: the hand-rolled stage emits none and the library emits `"max_level":3`, so in that pack this mod's research becomes a three-level technology whose unlock fires at level one and whose other levels are no-ops a player pays for. Graded **AWKWARD**.
- **A `count_formula` source now loads, and used to abort.** The three-field read produced a unit with neither `count` nor `count_formula` and the engine refused: `Error while loading technology prototype "bbb-balancer" (technology): Key "count_formula" not found in property tree at ROOT.technology.bbb-balancer.unit`, rc=1. The verbatim copy loads, rc=0. An IMPROVEMENT, and the same library decision as the two above seen from the third side.

All three are pinned by host tests against a fixture World, so a change in any of them shows up without an engine.

Measured, base only: `logistics-2` is 200 units over 30 s and `logistics-3` is 300 over 15 s, and the gate asserts each against that technology's OWN unit in the same dump rather than against a figure transcribed here -- which is the only comparison that stays true the day base re-costs a tier.

### The belt speed, and the claim that was wrong for five milestones

**`hiddenSpeed` was 0.25 from M2 to 0.3.0 and this file called it a CEILING.** It is not. The measurement: a belt faster than 0.25 runs FULLY COMPRESSED and delivers **480 x speed items/s**, so a modded belt above 120 items/s was silently throttled to 120 at every port of every balancer -- which is what the portal's "Turbo-belts" ask was about. The false ceiling claim is purged from `hidden.go` rather than corrected in place.

0.25 is a **FLOOR** now, and `deriveHiddenSpeed` at `data-final-fixes` raises the four hidden prototypes to the fastest belt any loaded mod defines. The scan is `fkdata.Keys` per belt family and one leaf `Get` per member -- the sorted-enumeration primitive's whole purpose, because a `pairs()` walk over `data.raw["transport-belt"]` is insertion order and a data stage that branched on one would be a join refusal nobody can reproduce. Seven families (`transport-belt`, `underground-belt`, `splitter`, `lane-splitter`, `loader`, `loader-1x1`, `linked-belt`), all descending from `TransportBeltConnectablePrototype` where `speed` is mandatory. About thirty host calls, once per game load, and nothing on any tick.

**THERE IS NO UPPER CAP AND THERE MUST NOT BE ONE.** Every candidate is a value the engine ALREADY ACCEPTED, on the very prototype it was read from: a belt-connectable's `speed` is validated when that mod's prototype loads, so mirroring it onto four more prototypes of the same families cannot reach a value the loader would refuse. A cap would be this mod second-guessing a number Factorio validated, and it would re-introduce the throttle for exactly the player who installed the fast belt. A NaN is ignored, and that is a property of `>` rather than a guard.

**The ordering caveat, stated rather than hidden**: `data-final-fixes` is the LAST stage there is, so the scan sees every belt every mod defined at data, data-updates and final-fixes-before-us. A mod whose own `data-final-fixes` runs AFTER this one and raises a belt then is missed, and there is nowhere later to move to. The cost for that one player is the old behaviour: the network at the second-fastest belt's speed.

**Our own four clones are IN the scan, at the floor, and that is deliberate.** They are `transport-belt`, `splitter`, `lane-splitter` and `linked-belt` prototypes, so the families enumerate them. It is not a ratchet -- `data.raw` is rebuilt on every load, so the clone is at the floor again next time and the maximum is a function of the installed mods alone. Excluding them would be a name filter that has to stay in step with `hidden.go`, to change an answer the floor already covers. **The floor is not made redundant by that**, and the red proof below is why: lowering `SpeedFloor` lowers the creation value too, so the whole thing follows it down.

### Red-proven three times, and the three catch different things

| injected defect | what fired |
|---|---|
| **the existence guard deleted** from `tune.Resolve` (with a plan pointing at a Space-Age-only belt, so a base-only game lacks it) | the unit test names every unproven ingredient in every option, and the `recipe-belt-express` gate arm dies on the ENGINE's own `Error in assignID: item with name 'turbo-transport-belt' does not exist.` -- `--dump-data exited 1`. **With the guard IN PLACE and the same plan the arm is green**, stepping past the missing rung to `express-transport-belt`: that control is what makes this a proof of the guard rather than of the plan |
| **the floor dropped** from 0.25 to 0.125 in `tune.SpeedFloor` | three unit-test failures, and **BOTH golden `data_raw_sha256` arms move** -- the four hidden prototypes come out at 0.125, half the speed the whole estate was measured on. The SPEED arm stays green, correctly: 0.5 beats either floor. That division is the point -- the goldens are the no-change proof and the speed arm is the change proof |
| **the vanilla default drifted** (iron-plate 4 -> 3) | `TestVanillaIsTodaysRecipe` names both lists, BOTH golden `data_raw_sha256` arms move, and the `recipe-vanilla` gate arm prints the drifted list against the expected one. Three independent detectors for the one change that would invalidate every recorded number in this repository |

**The first row's `tune.Resolve` is deleted since round two of the FkRecipes migration** and the guard it names is the library's, so that proof is a record of what was measured in 0.3.1 rather than one that can be repeated as written. The other two are unchanged and both were re-run in round two: the default drifting still fires three detectors, and the speed floor is not a library concern at all.

### The settings are declared through FkRecipes since 2026-09-01, and the prototypes followed in round two

**The two startup dropdowns moved onto [FkRecipes](https://github.com/Techrocket9/FkRecipes), the shared data-stage library, in round one; the item, the recipe and the technology followed in round two, and `guest/go/data/item.go`, `recipe.go` and `technology.go` are deleted.** Neither half is a staging decision. Round one's prototype arm was written, run and REFUSED BY THE ENGINE, and it is recorded below as the measurement it was; round two moved on a library that had answered every one of the three refusals by name. `guest/go/tune/plan.go` is the plan and its header is the long form; [`agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`](agents/fkrecipes-migration.md) is both runs and the graded friction list.

**What migrated is two calls.** `lib.LegacyDropdownSettingNeedingLocale(SettingRecipeCost, RecipeDefault(), RecipeOptions(), "a")` and the same for `SettingTechCost` at `"b"`, and `guest/go/data/settings.go`'s whole part in them is `tune.Plan().Emit()`. **`Legacy` is forced rather than preferred**: Factorio persists a player's startup choices in `mod-settings.dat` keyed by the setting's NAME and has no rename mechanism, so a prefixed `better-belt-balancer-bbb-recipe-cost` would be a NEW setting and every player who had chosen a value would silently get the default. The order strings are this mod's own for the same reason -- a generated order is two letters from declaration order, and `order` is a field in the settings dump.

**EACH HOOK NAMES THE HALF IT RUNS SINCE ROUND TWO.** `Emit` reads the running stage and dispatches at RUN TIME, so a guest that calls it links both planners whatever its plan declares -- which is where round one's 21,047-line unreachable function came from. `guest/go/data/main.go` calls `EmitSettings` from `fk_settings` and `EmitData` from `fk_data`, nothing calls `Emit`, and each of the two raises if it is routed from the wrong stage. `fk_data_final_fixes` does not mention the library.

**What round one measured out, and what answered it.** Three things stopped the prototype half then and the first was fatal on its own; all three are library surface now:

| round one measured | round two has |
|---|---|
| **every prototype name carried the mod prefix**, with no Legacy constructor for one: `bbb-balancer-part` became `better-belt-balancer-bbb-balancer-part` and `entity.go`'s `minable.result` then named an item nobody defined -- `Error in assignID: item with name 'bbb-balancer-part' does not exist. Source: bbb-balancer-part (simple-entity-with-force).`, `--dump-data exited 1` | `LegacyItem`, `LegacyRecipe` and `LegacyTechnology`, which emit a shipped name VERBATIM. The argument is the Legacy settings' with a wider blast radius: a prototype name is held by blueprints, logistic requests, crafting queues and other mods' patches, and no single dump says whether anything is holding one |
| **`ItemSpec`, `RecipeSpec` and `TechSpec` carried no `order`**, so the item's and the recipe's `c[splitter]-y[bbb-balancer]` and the technology's `a-b-bbb` were DROPPED -- which moves this mod's row in every crafting menu and in Factoriopedia | an `Order` field on all three |
| **`ItemSpec` carried no `place_result`**, the one field that makes the item place the entity | `PlaceResult`, PRESENCE PROBED against the entity types. That probe is what fixes the order of the `fk_data` hook: `entity()` first, `EmitData` after it, or the plan is refused by name |

So all three prototypes are declarations in `guest/go/tune/plan.go` and the three files that built them are deleted. **The recipe and the technology had to cross in ONE commit** and the reason is none of the three above: the library emits a recipe's `enabled` as "no technology in THIS PLAN unlocks me", `RecipeSpec` has no `Enabled` field, and `Extra` refuses a key the library emits itself -- so a recipe declared while its technology is still hand-rolled comes out `enabled = true`, craftable from the first minute, and moves the data hash.

**And the two verbs this mod wanted the library for are the ones it now uses.** `IngredientsBy` takes one `IngredientChoice` per allowed value of `bbb-recipe-cost`, each ingredient an `IngredientNamed` ladder built from `tune.RecipePlan` rung for rung; `CostBy` takes one `CostChoice` per value of `bbb-tech-cost` whose sources are `tune.TechLadder`, and it carries the prerequisite with the unit, which is the rule this mod wrote by hand. `tune` keeps the ladders and stops walking them.

**THREE BEHAVIOURS MOVED WITH `CostBy` AND ALL THREE ARE ON THE RECORD**: the fallback's science pack was probed even when the fallback was unreachable (a load that used to succeed and refused, AWKWARD, and CLOSED by FkRecipes c7a806e on 2026-09-07: the bullet under "The technology, where the prerequisite moves with the unit" carries the closure), `max_level` travels with the copied unit (a single-recipe technology becoming multi-level in a pack whose source is, AWKWARD), and a `count_formula` source that used to abort the load now loads (an improvement). Each is measured on the engine and pinned by a host test; "The technology, where the prerequisite moves with the unit" is the long form.

**AND THE UNKNOWN-OPTION ARM OF `RecipePlan` AND `TechLadder` IS A SHAPE GUARD RATHER THAN A LIVE FALLBACK.** [Plan] builds one choice per allowed value, so an unknown stored value reaches the library rather than this package's default. Round two's library answered it with a recipe made of no ingredients and a fallback-priced technology; **since FkRecipes c7a806e the library REFUSES it BY NAME**, `fkrecipes: bbb-recipe-cost holds "not-an-option", which is not one of its values`, and the same for `bbb-tech-cost` -- the emitted name, which for this mod's two Legacy settings is the unprefixed one a player's file carries. What makes that unreachable is the ENGINE: an unknown value in `mod-settings.dat` is silently RESET to the default before the data stage runs (measured on both packages, no log line), and a wrong TYPE is refused loudly. Both comments say so now, the test that asserted the dead arm is deleted, and `TestAnUnofferedStoredValueIsRefusedByName` pins the refusal on both dropdowns behind the engine's guard.

**THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS BOTH GOLDEN HASHES NOT MOVING, AND THEY DID NOT.** `make datastage-check`, Factorio 2.0.77, eleven arms green: `base data_raw_sha256 f4fbcaa603abc93b`, `base mod_settings_sha256 196275f867f7f8b5`, `incumbent data_raw_sha256 e7001bf98d6c6771`, `incumbent mod_settings_sha256 196275f867f7f8b5`, plus all eight variant arms and the speed arm. (Round three MOVED `mod_settings_sha256` on purpose, twice, and `data_raw_sha256` not at all; the current hashes are in "Round three" and in the Verification table.) **The 2.1.16 and 2.1.17 golden rows are NOT RUN**: the installed binary is 2.0.77 and the packaged mod is pinned 2.1, so a golden whose engine does not match the binary is a SKIP by construction and `make test` refuses at its engine gate for the same reason.

**And the plan is pinned a second way, on the host.** `go test ./tune/` compares every field of both emitted prototypes against literals TRANSCRIBED from the pre-migration dump rather than derived from `RecipeOptions()` and `TechOptions()` -- a gate that computed its answer from the same source as the thing under test would agree with a defect in that source. Keys compare order-insensitively (fkdata sorts them out anyway) and `allowed_values` compares IN ORDER, because that order is the order of the rows in the settings menu. The two instruments answer different questions: the hash says nothing moved, the field comparison says WHICH one did.

### What round two cost, and the like-for-like control that makes it readable

**THE COMPARISON THAT MEANS ANYTHING IS AGAINST ROUND ONE'S CODE REBUILT ON TODAY'S LIBRARY**, not against round one's recorded figures. FkRecipes moved six commits between the two rounds and grew every one of the surfaces round two consumes, so a straight before/after would credit round two with the library's growth or blame it for it. So round one's `guest/go/data`, `guest/go/tune` and `Makefile` were checked out **into the real tree, at the real path**, built from `make clean`, measured, and put back. Both builds are Factorio 2.0.77, FkRecipes `b43c2c7`, FkLua `32eb628`, TinyGo 0.41.1, shipped config.

**`PlanData` is 23,288 emitted Lua lines, 32.9% of the module, and it is the LIBRARY'S growth rather than this plan's.** Round one's code on the same library is **23,493**, so round two is 205 lines under it; the move from round one's recorded 21,047 is entirely FkRecipes between `b43c2c7` and what round one measured. It is 82.8% of the 28,139-line function that once failed Lua 5.2's parser with `control structure too long near 'trap_unreachable'`, no jump-span advisory fired, and **the consumer still has no remedy**: the `//go:noinline` discipline `guest/go/data/main.go` carries cannot be applied to somebody else's package. **The settings stage got cheaper and the data stage pays for the whole plan.** A 6.8% smaller module is parsed three times, which is where the settings saving comes from; against it, `data.lua` now runs `PlanData` for real -- the ingredient and entity presence probes, the cycle walk over every technology in the game, and the emit -- where round one ran three hand-rolled builders and about a dozen probes. **Net, about fourteen milliseconds per game load**, once per load, on a path with no tick in it.

**THERE IS NO HOST-CALL COUNTER AND THE NUMBER IS NOT ESTIMATED HERE.** Neither `fklua mod`'s report nor Factorio's log counts the calls a data stage makes, and `fkdata` keeps no counter, so what the cycle walk costs is visible only as the 23 ms above. The shape is in the library's own source -- `checkCycles` reads `TechNames()` once and `TechPrereqs(name)` once per technology -- and this file does not put a figure on it, because a figure derived from somebody else's source and a technology count is arithmetic rather than a measurement.

**The go.mod facts, because two of them look wrong and are not.** `github.com/Techrocket9/fklua/guest/go` moved **v0.0.0 -> v0.2.0**: FkRecipes requires that tag through the real channel and minimal version selection takes the maximum, so the number is not a choice made here and the `replace` still resolves it onto `../../../FkLua/guest/go`. The FkRecipes `replace` is **DEV-ONLY** and marked so: there is no remote and no tag, and `v0.1.0` is the tag its README names as its eventual Go one. **There is no `go.sum` and none is created**, which is what a directory replace means. `go mod tidy` DELETES an unimported require, so the dependency and its first import have to land in one edit.

**And `make check`'s data-guest vet line carried `-tags tinygo.wasm` in round one and does not any more.** FkRecipes' emit layer -- `Emit` itself -- is behind `//go:build tinygo.wasm`, a tag TinyGo's wasm-unknown target sets and the standard toolchain does not, so without it the vet failed on `....Emit undefined (type *fkrecipes.Lib has no field or method Emit)` in the one gate that exists to catch compile errors. The library ships HOST STUBS for `Emit`, `EmitSettings` and `EmitData` now (`go/guest_host.go`, which panic naming the cause), so the ordinary toolchain type-checks the data guest exactly as it type-checks everything else here and the flag is gone.

**AND THE MAKEFILE TRACKS FkRecipes' OWN SOURCES SINCE ROUND TWO, because it is consumed from a WORKING TREE.** `DATA_GUEST_SRC` listed this repository's files alone, so an edit next door changed what the data guest links and moved nothing `make` could see. Measured: round two's baseline `make datastage-check` came back green over a `dist/bbbdata.wasm` that `make mod` had declined to rebuild against a library six commits newer. FkLua's `guest/go` is deliberately NOT tracked the same way: the hazard is the same, its pin moves through `fklua.lock` and `gen-bindings --check`, and one dependency at a time is one change at a time.

### Round three, 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08: a Custom value on both dropdowns, and the plan is six settings

**THIS SECTION IS A DATED RECORD AND ITS HEADLINE IS SUPERSEDED BY FIX ROUND 2, 2026-09-14.** There is no `custom` value on either dropdown any more: FkRecipes `6518971` withdrew it and moved the state into the text field beside the dropdown, so the six presets and the three tiers are the whole of what each setting allows and the four generated settings decide by not being at their declared defaults. **Both dropdowns gain one value, `custom`, LAST, and four settings arrive beside them.** `bbb-recipe-cost` on `custom` takes the ingredients from `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` (round three's `bbb-recipe-ingredients`; the four customizer names are generated since the sync pass), a text field in FkRecipes' ingredient language (`3 iron-plate, 1 splitter`; the reference is FkRecipes' docs/ingredient-list.md). `bbb-tech-cost` on `custom` takes the research unit from `better-belt-balancer-tech-packs` (the same language, science packs only), `better-belt-balancer-tech-count` (an int, 1 to 1,000,000) and `better-belt-balancer-tech-seconds` (a double, 1 to 3600), and hangs the technology off the first of `logistics`, `logistics-2`, `logistics-3` the game has (the tier list itself since fix round 1, so an untouched Custom hangs where the default tier hangs), or off nothing with a line saying so. The six presets and the three tiers keep their spelling, their order and their positions, so every stored preference reads as it did; the two text fields ship holding the word `default`, which means this mod's own list WITH its ladders in this release and every later one; the research fields default to [FallbackUnit], 20 automation science over 15 s, so picking Custom and typing nothing changes the price of nothing in a game that has `automation-science-pack`. **In a game that does not, Custom untouched is a REFUSAL where every tier still loads**: the declared pack list carries no `Fallbacks` ladder (argued in `plan.go`: no science pack is a name every game has, so a second rung would be a guess dressed as a ladder), the library drops a pack the game lacks and refuses a unit that has lost every pack (`fkrecipes: the technology bbb-balancer has no science pack the game has; research takes at least one`), and a tier copies its source's own unit and never asks. **AND THAT REFUSAL IS GONE SINCE FkRecipes `97a4493`, 2026-09-14**, which is the one sentence of this dated record that describes an outcome rather than a shape: a technology that loses every science pack is EMITTED with an empty unit, the load completes, one `fkrecipes: ERROR: ` line names every rung the walk asked the game about, and the technology's own description says it takes no science pack at all. What the player gets there is a FREE research, which is a balance change nobody chose and is disclosed rather than good. README says the outcome in the player's terms; see `agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`, "Fix round 3". ### Fix round 2, 2026-09-14: the library withdraws the Custom value, and the text beside the dropdown is the switch

**The long form, every measurement and every red proof, is [`agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`](agents/fkrecipes-migration.md), "Fix round 2"; the assessment it answers is [`agents/migration-assessment-2.md`](agents/migration-assessment-2.md), and the scope every grade in it is made against is FkRecipes' own [`../FkRecipes/agents/threat-model.md`](../FkRecipes/agents/threat-model.md), whose governing sentence is THE LOG IS NOT WHERE A PLAYER LOOKS.** FkRecipes moved five commits, `21f5d89` to `221ff9c`; FkLua is unmoved as a pin and its checkout is at `01d640a`, `fklua.lock` untouched, `gen-bindings --check` and `lock --check` both exit 0, api pin still 2.1.17. **THIS IS THE ROUND'S FOURTH COMMIT AND IT IS NOT THE LAST.** The adopt commit, the locale prose, the labels and the changelog, and the remover fixture have all landed; a defect in the LIBRARY that the fixture's own red proofs turned up, and then the round's close, are owed after them.

**THE STATE MOVED OUT OF A DROPDOWN VALUE AND INTO THE FIELD A PLAYER TYPES, AND THE OPTION LISTS DID NOT MOVE AT ALL.** `bbb-recipe-cost` allows the same six values it has always allowed and `bbb-tech-cost` the same three; `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` applies whenever it does not say the reserved word `default`, and each of `better-belt-balancer-tech-packs`, `-tech-count` and `-tech-seconds` overwrites the chosen tier's unit ONE FIELD AT A TIME, a pack text on the word and a number at 0 meaning "the tier decides this one". **The reason is finding 3 measured**: Factorio RESETS a stored dropdown value the running release's `allowed_values` does not list and PERSISTS the reset with no line in the log, while a setting a release does not declare survives verbatim, so a `custom` row was destroyed by one launch of an older release while the typed text beside it lived. Adopting the customizer on a dropdown a mod already ships is an IDENTITY in this shape: no stored choice is reset or changes meaning, and a rollback loses nothing. `custom` never shipped in a public release of this mod, so the withdrawal costs no player anything here.

**FOUR DECLARATIONS STOPPED COMPILING AND ALL FOUR ARE IN `tune.Plan()`**, which is where the library's own adoption list said they would be. `IngredientChoices.Custom` becomes `RecipeSpec.IngredientsFrom` one level out; `CostChoices.Custom` becomes `TechSpec.CostFrom`; `CustomCost.Position` is gone with no replacement and none needed, because every value of `bbb-tech-cost` names a source technology and that source is the prerequisite whatever the three fields say, so a cost cannot come apart from its place; and `CustomCost.Seconds` takes an `IntSettingRef`, so `lib.DoubleSetting(TechSecondsName, 15, ...)` became `lib.IntSetting(TechSecondsName, 0, Between(0, 3600))`. **TWO MORE ARE LOAD FAILURES RATHER THAN BUILD FAILURES** and arrive after the compiler is happy: the choice list must cover the dropdown's `allowed_values` EXACTLY, so `RecipeValues`, `TechValues`, `RecipeCustom` and `TechCustom` are DELETED OUTRIGHT rather than reduced to aliases (the whole reason the Options/Values split existed was the seventh value and the fourth, and one list per dropdown is now read by the declaration, by the choice builder and by every test); and a research count or seconds beside a `CostBy` must declare default 0 and minimum 0, so this mod's 20-with-minimum-1 and 15-with-minimum-1 are both 0. **The maxima are still this mod's and the minima are not**: the library refuses a research number with no maximum of at least 1, so 1,000,000 and 3,600 are the one bound left to choose and are unchanged. What stops a 0 reaching the engine is the cost behind the field rather than the fence: a field at 0 emits the tier's number, or `CostChoices.Fallback`'s where no source in the ladder carries a unit.

**THE SUITE IS FIFTY-THREE TESTS, thirteen gone and twelve new** (`cd guest/go && go test ./tune/ -count=1`, exit 0; `-v | grep -c '^=== RUN   Test'` reads 53, where the re-adoption leg's was 54). Eleven of the twelve are the adopt commit's and the twelfth is the locale commit's `TestNoSettingDescriptionNamesAnOptionNoDropdownOffers`, below. Four of the thirteen had nothing left to assert: `TestAnEditedTextUnderAPresetIsIgnoredAndTheLogSaysSo` and `TestAnEditedPackTextUnderATierIsIgnoredAndTheLogSaysSo` pinned `... is edited, but ... is not on custom, so the text is ignored`, a sentence that exists nowhere in the library now because every non-default value is live; `TestThePositionLadderStepsUpAndThenLetsGo` and `TestTheCustomArmTakesItsPlaceFromTheDefaultTier` were about `CustomCost.Position` and have no API behind them. Eight of the other nine are RENAMED as well as rewritten, because a name is an assertion too, and the sharpest is `TestTheCustomResearchCostUntouchedIsTheFallbackUnit` becoming `TestTheThreeFieldsUntouchedLeaveTheTierDeciding`: what an untouched research field means moved from "this mod's own 20 and 15" to "whatever the tier charges". **`CheckLocaleAdvisories` IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED INTO ANY FAILING TEST**, which is the library's item 7 and a prohibition rather than a suggestion: it returns a note per out-of-prefix key whether or not the file defines it, it never goes away, and what it asks for is that nothing be done, so a suite failing on it would be permanently red over a thing the library says not to fix. Its three notes are `t.Log`ged by `TestTheLocaleFileRenamesNoTechnologyOfTheGames`, which ASSERTS the thing this mod can get wrong: that the `.cfg` defines no `[technology-name]` entry but its own.

**REMEDY (f) OF THIS MOD'S SECOND ASSESSMENT IS NOT DONE AND IS NOW ACTIVELY WRONG.** It said to define `technology-name.logistics-2` and `-3` here so the research-cost tooltip would not lose itself to an undefined key. FkRecipes `e4604d4` closed that from the library's end -- every composed key goes out as `{"?", {"<section>.<key>"}, "<raw>"}`, so an undefined key degrades to the raw internal name and the tooltip survives whole -- and carrying out (f) today would set the displayed name of BASE's technologies for every mod in the game, Factorio's locale namespace being flat and shared. The new test is what keeps it undone.

**THE GOLDEN MOVED IN EXACTLY THE SHAPE THE LIBRARY PREDICTED, AND THIS REPOSITORY CHECKED THE PREDICTION BEFORE RE-CAPTURING.** `mod_settings_sha256` only, `aa75497e55ce4333` to `b6e583e6163249ba`, the same on both mod sets; both `data_raw_sha256` unmoved to the digit (`1e1fcf4f56f5ef22` base, `e7001bf98d6c6771` incumbent) and both `prototype_list_checksum` values with them, and since the data-raw hash is taken over the whole normalised dump its being unmoved IS those dumps compared byte for byte. Five things moved in the settings dump, every one read out of the engine's own `mod-settings-dump.json`: `allowed_values` six where it was seven and three where it was four; `better-belt-balancer-tech-seconds` an `int-setting` where it was a `double-setting` under the same name, with both research numbers at default 0 and minimum 0; both dropdowns' composed description gaining a closing switch line and the ingredient one the wrap line before it, both text settings gaining the wrap line and a switch line, and the ingredient one's format line gaining the `none` clause (finding 18 and remedy (g)); the two research numbers carrying a composed description where they carried NONE AT ALL, which is half of finding 9 (the two numeric ranges are in words where a player looks now); and every locale key inside a composed description wrapped in the engine's alternatives form, which is finding 15 -- the research-cost setting had NO TOOLTIP AT ALL on a stock install and no gate in either repository could see it, because `--dump-data` carries the string whether or not it draws.

**THE COMPOSED TOOLTIPS, RE-MEASURED ON THE ENGINE WITH THIS MOD'S OWN `.cfg` RESOLVED INTO THEM**, six settings where four carried a description before: `bbb-recipe-cost` 9 parameters, depth 4, 15 lines, longest **557**, 1,323 characters; `bbb-tech-cost` 5, depth 4, 5 lines, longest **622**, 885; `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` 6, depth 3, 6 lines, longest 420, 967; `-tech-packs` 6, depth 3, 6 lines, longest 409, 862; `-tech-count` and `-tech-seconds` 2, depth 3, 2 lines, longest 105 and 117, 186 and 195. **THE CEILINGS FIX ROUND 1 QUOTED WERE WRONG IN ONE HALF AND ARE CORRECTED**: FkRecipes re-measured both on 2.0.77 this cycle and they are **20 PARAMETERS PER TABLE** (not per string; the 21st refuses with `Too many parameters for localised string: 21 > 20 (limit).`) and **20 LEVELS OF NESTING DEPTH** (the 21st refuses with `Too deep recursion for localised string: 21 > 20 (limit).`), with no global table budget at all. Nothing is near either. The 557 and the 622 are this mod's own two dropdown entries, and the locale commit cut them to 443 and 563 without re-measuring the composed wholes. **THAT RE-MEASUREMENT LANDED IN THE THIRD COMMIT RATHER THAN AT THE ROUND'S CLOSE**, because the labels move the same two tooltips: `bbb-recipe-cost` is **970** characters and `bbb-tech-cost` **733**, the other four unmoved to the byte, and the parameter, depth and line counts in the table above are unmoved as well. The figures here stand as the adopt commit's, on the shape it measured. **NOT MEASURED: whether any of the six renders whole.** No client was run and none was started, which is the client run owed since round three and now one line larger on four of the six.

**THE GATE IS TWENTY-ONE ARMS SINCE THIS ROUND'S FOURTH COMMIT, TWENTY FROM THE ADOPT COMMIT UNTIL THEN, AND ITS EIGHT CUSTOMIZER ARMS ARE NAMED FOR STATES RATHER THAN FOR A DROPDOWN VALUE**: `recipe-default-word`, `recipe-text-alone`, `recipe-text-over-preset`, `recipe-self-product`, `tech-cost-whole`, `tech-tier-word`, `tech-count-alone`, `tech-packs-alone`. Every one compares the whole `fkrecipes:` stream in order, which the seven before them could not, and every one was run once with `startup=None` -- the run a missing `.dat` produces byte for byte -- so each fails on a PROTOTYPE field and not only on a sentence if the file never arrived. `OUR_SETTINGS_ORDERS` does not move: `a`, `aab`, `b`, `bad`, `bae`, `baf`, because withdrawing a value moves neither a name nor an order. The twenty-first arm is the merge arm's second mod set, which the fourth commit added and which is not what remedy (i) asked for; the decomposition is 2 golden + 16 variant + 1 speed + 2 merge, read off the script's own constants rather than counted by eye. See Verification.

**RED-PROVEN EIGHT WAYS, every break in this mod's own code, fixture or locale file and never in a library**, which was read-only for the whole commit. Dropping `IngredientsBy` while keeping `IngredientsFrom` reddens TWELVE tests, including all four rows of `TestATextTheGameCannotAnswerFallsBackAndSaysSo`; removing `IngredientsFrom`, and separately `CostFrom`, reddens 38 each on the library's binding rule; swapping the `Count` and `Seconds` handles reddens exactly two tests, which is the narrowest pair in the suite; putting the fixture `World`'s stored `20` and `15` back reddens 21; putting `IntSetting(TechCountName, 20, Between(1, 1000000))` back reddens three on the library's designed refusal; adding `[technology-name] logistics-2=Belt logistics II` to the `.cfg` reddens the new locale test, which is the only thing in either repository that could have seen it; and flipping either of two boolean arguments in the test helpers reddens exactly one test per call site.

**TWO FINDINGS ABOUT THIS MOD'S OWN FIXTURE, AND NEITHER IS THE LIBRARY'S.** The fixture `World` stored `Num(20)` and `Num(15)` for the two research numbers, which were this mod's old declared defaults and are, under the new ones, a player who DRAGGED BOTH SLIDERS -- so every test meaning to drive an untouched game would have been driving an overridden one, and the numbers it drove look exactly like an untouched field. And `TestAnUnreachedFallbacksPackIsNeverProbed` was silently wrong: `67b5090` filters a COPIED tier unit's own packs through `ToolExists`, so the world that took every tool away now loses the tier's pack as well and lands on a refusal, which is the opposite of the test's name. Its world is `logistics-2` in a game whose only tool is `logistic-science-pack`, and the claim is sharper for being narrower.

**ONE THING OWED UPSTREAM.** When a chosen tier's copied pack and the declared `Fallback`'s one rung are the same name, `67b5090`'s new rung list names it twice: `... research takes at least one, and none of automation-science-pack, automation-science-pack is a science pack here`. Two tests here reach it and pin it as it is. It is cosmetic, it is in a sentence a player reads in an error dialog, and the fix is a de-duplication in the library's walk. **CLOSED 2026-09-14 BY FkRecipes `f2df7ab`**, which moved the de-duplication to the single writer of the state the sentence is composed from; the two tests went red by name, which is what they were pinned for, and pin the single-name sentence now. See "Fix round 2b re-adoption" below.

**THE ROUND'S SECOND COMMIT IS THE TEN ENTRIES, AND ITS SUBJECT IS A DEFECT NOTHING ANYWHERE COULD GO RED OVER.** Six `[mod-setting-description]` and four `[mod-setting-name]` entries named an option the dropdown no longer offers, and all ten are rewritten under ONE RULE: the text field applies whenever it does not say `default`, and the dropdown supplies the rest. For the research that rule is PER FIELD, the pack text switching on the word and the two numbers on 0. Seven comment blocks move with them, `bbb-recipe-cost` goes 557 characters to 443 and `bbb-tech-cost` 622 to 563, and TWO ENTRIES GOT SHORTER BY DROPPING A SENTENCE THE LIBRARY NOW COMPOSES ONTO THE SAME TOOLTIP. **ONE OF THOSE TWO OMISSIONS WAS WRONG, AND AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEW CAUGHT IT WHERE NO GATE COULD**: `bbb-tech-cost`'s three fields were dropped on the theory that the library says so, and what the library composes there is `The setting below applies instead while it does not say default.`, which is SINGULAR, is built from `CustomCost.Packs` alone (`go/customize.go:680`), and switches on a word where two of the three fields switch on 0. ### Fix round 2b re-adoption, 2026-09-14: the sentence that stopped the load is two elements now, and 0.3.3 is unblocked

**The long form, every measurement and every red proof, is [`agents/fkrecipes-migration.md`](agents/fkrecipes-migration.md), "Fix round 2b re-adoption".** FkRecipes `221ff9c` to `61ac80c`, three commits, and the block this mod's previous round ended on lifts on the middle one.

**THE BLOCK LIFTS ON `137f4aa` AND ON A RUN RATHER THAN ON A CLAIM.** The library chunks every literal it composes into a DATA-STAGE PROTOTYPE's `localised_name` or `localised_description` into elements of at most 180 bytes, cut after the last space inside the budget, concatenation byte-identical. The SETTINGS side is deliberately not chunked and that is a rule rather than an oversight, a setting prototype being exempt from the ceiling by measurement (5000-byte elements load), so this mod's four composed setting descriptions are untouched by the whole round. The engine joins a localised string's parameters with nothing between them, so the bytes a player's client is handed are the bytes it was handed before; whether a chunk boundary shows on SCREEN is unmeasured and is below. Measured here on 2.0.77 build 84539, this package and base alone, with `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` storing `2 iron-plat`, which is the text the previous round measured the refusal on: **exit 0 and a dump** where it was exit 1 and none; `bbb-balancer-part.localised_description` **exactly three elements**, `""` then 176 bytes ending `... Changing a recipe empties an ` with the trailing space then 71 bytes reading `assembling machine's input slots of anything the new list does not use.`, which concatenate to the 247-byte sentence byte for byte and end with the same destruction sentence the log line ends with; **exactly one `fkrecipes: ERROR: ` line**, now a line somebody can read; and **the recipe is the dropdown's own default**, 4 iron plates, 2 gears and 2 transport belts, which is what a player who typed nothing gets and is the claim the library's whole player-fallback design rests on, measured on an engine through this mod for the first time. The technology channel is unchanged and is still the control: 138 bytes in ONE element on `bbb-balancer`, inside the library's own budget, with the recipe in that load carrying nothing.

**THE TWO DOCUMENTS THE PREVIOUS ROUND DECLINED TO REWRITE WERE RE-READ AGAINST THAT RUN AND ARE TRUE AS THEY STAND**, so both are kept: the 0.3.3 changelog's Info row on a typo setting a list aside, and `README.md`'s "The game loads, so you can correct the field and restart." Neither gains a sentence about the tooltip, which is a decision: where that line wraps in a real crafting screen is unmeasured, and the log sentence is the one this repository has measured.

**THREE TESTS WENT RED ON THE UNTOUCHED TREE AND ALL THREE WERE PINNED TO.** `TestATextTheGameCannotAnswerFallsBackAndSaysSo` expected the note in one element and got two, which is the chunker arriving; `TestAFallbackThisModsOwnPackListCannotPayForStillRefuses` and `TestAPackTheGameHasOnlyAsAnItemIsDroppedAndThenRefused` expected `... none of automation-science-pack, automation-science-pack is a science pack here` and got the name once, which is `f2df7ab` de-duplicating the rung list and is the item the previous round's own still-open list said would fail here by name. **THOSE TWO WERE RENAMED IN FIX ROUND 3 WITH THE REFUSAL THEY PINNED**: they are `TestAFallbackThisModsOwnPackListCannotPayForIsEmittedFreeBesideTheSetAsideText` and `TestAPackTheGameHasOnlyAsAnItemIsDroppedAndTheResearchIsEmittedFree`, and what they pin is an emitted free research rather than a stopped load. **NO EXECUTABLE GUEST SOURCE CHANGED IN THIS LEG**, which is shown rather than asserted: `guest/go/tune/plan.go` is the only guest file touched and `git diff -U0 -- guest/go/tune/plan.go | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^[+-][+-]' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*//'` is EMPTY, which is the evidence FkRecipes' own `61ac80c` gives for the same kind of claim. The rest is tests, the gate and documentation, so the packaged mod differs from the previous round's only through the library.

**`checkFallbackNote` ASKS THREE SEPARATELY BREAKABLE QUESTIONS NOW** instead of one equality: every element at or under the engine's 200 bytes (the number that decides whether the game loads, compared against and never computed with), the elements concatenated being the sentence byte for byte (which says the chunking is invisible to a reader), and the cut falling where this library head puts it (pinned deliberately, and named in the helper as the weakest of the three).

**THE GATE ARM IS INVERTED AND IS `note-recipe`.** `note-refused` asserted a return code, an engine refusal and the library's line present in a run that produced no dump; its own block said twice what to do on the day it went red, and the remedy is carried out rather than deleted. It asserts the library's ERROR line unchanged, the element COUNT, the two chunks whole, **every element against the 200-byte ceiling over what the ENGINE put in the dump** rather than over the literal beside it, the TECHNOLOGY in that load carrying nothing (the mirror of what `note-control` already said about the recipe), and the RECIPE ITSELF. The rename is because a row reading `note-refused exit 0` would read as a contradiction: what is refused is the TEXT, which is the premise of both arms rather than the outcome of either. `note-control` keeps its name and every measurement. **The arm count does not move, twenty-three.** `expect_refusal` is GONE from `run_arm` with the defect it existed for, being the one opt-out from this file's rule that a non-zero engine exit stops the whole gate and having no caller left.

**NO GOLDEN MOVED AND NONE WAS RE-CAPTURED**, `1e1fcf4f56f5ef22`, `e7001bf98d6c6771` and `b6e583e6163249ba` all reading at HEAD exactly what the previous round captured, which is what a chunker reached only by a composed note should do. **THE RELEASE-TO-HEAD PROOF WAS RE-RUN AND IS A STRONGER COMPARISON THAN BEFORE**: fourteen configurations on both mod sets, 28 pairs, each pair one `--dump-data` against the mod built on `221ff9c` and one against the same tree built on `61ac80c`, comparing THE WHOLE NORMALISED DUMP rather than an owned-prototype extract. **All 28 IDENTICAL on both hashes, zero DIFFERS, no log stream moved, exit 0.** The old half was built with `git archive` out of FkRecipes into a scratch directory and a one-build `replace`, so nothing in either sibling checkout was written.

**THIRTEEN RED PROOFS, all in this mod's own tree because FkRecipes is read-only**, each break observed and each file restored and sha256-compared afterwards. THREE in the host suite: the helper's asserted ceiling narrowed to 150, its expected chunks collapsed to the whole sentence (the equality alone, the concatenation check staying green, which says the two are independent), and a word of its sentence mistyped. TEN in the engine gate, every one a full `make datastage-check` at exit 2: the asserted ceiling narrowed to 150 and again to 100 (the second says the check reaches the control arm too), the expected count collapsed to two, a word moved inside a chunk, the arm given a second falling-back setting, the arm's dropdown moved off its default, the expected sentence mistyped, **the shared destruction sentence changed, which reddens the TOOLTIP and the LOG on separate lines and is the one assertion two literals updated in step could not fake**, the technology-exists probe pointed at a name no mod defines, and the control arm's own sentence mistyped, which prints `note-recipe`'s ok row beside `note-control`'s failure and is the proof that each arm's summary is a function of that arm. **THE CEILING CANNOT BE BROKEN FROM THIS TREE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND THAT IS SAID PLAINLY**: the library's chunker bounds every element by construction, so the proof available is the reachability one.

**THE LIBRARY ROUND COSTS THE PACKAGED MOD NOTHING, MEASURED UNDER CONTROL, AND THE CROSS-ROUND SIZE COMPARISON IS WITHDRAWN.** One tree, one root, one packager, one toolchain and the ONLY variable the library head, each head `git archive`d into a scratch directory of the same path length: the **zip and `fk_data_module.lua` are BYTE-IDENTICAL across `221ff9c` and `61ac80c`** (`cmp` exit 0 on both), `dist/bbb.wasm` is unmoved, and the only thing that moves is `dist/bbbdata.wasm`, +6,688 B, which is not a package member. This leg's absolutes at the shipping root, which is what a future round should compare against: zip **892,437 B**, `fk_data_module.lua` **4,873,227 B and 124,177 lines**, `fk_module.lua` **3,132,893 B and 88,844 lines** (the FIFTH recorded point at which it is unmoved), `dist/bbb.wasm` **1,303,099 B**, `dist/bbbdata.wasm` **1,209,509 B**. **FIX ROUND 2'S CLOSE RECORDED 895,111, 4,992,501 / 128,322 AND 1,225,590 AND NOTHING HERE REPRODUCES THEM**, so the round-over-round series has a BREAK at this point and no delta is claimed across it; the library, the `replace` path, this leg's own comment edit and the packager binary were each ruled out with a build apiece, and what is not ruled out is named in the migration notes with the command that would close it. A first draft of this subsection attributed a -119,274 B module change to the library, which the controlled table falsifies, and the adversarial review before this commit is what made it measurable. Relay: stations **11** unmoved, the widest span 965,409 to **963,336 B**, the top-level after-relay 347,663 to **347,517**, and **the block room unmoved at 318,819 B** for the third round running, with the control guest unmoved in every field.

**THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT MOVE AND THE BINARY WAS DELIBERATELY NOT REBUILT.** `fklua.lock` untouched, api pin still 2.1.17, bindings unmoved, and `../FkLua/bin/fklua` is the previous round's own at `vcs.revision=01d640a...`, `vcs.modified=false`; FkLua's CHECKOUT moved `01d640a` to `16f0986` and `git diff --stat` says that is `agents/engine-findings.md | 2 +-` and nothing else, so a rebuild would change the revision string in the report and nothing in the output.

**`make test` and the 2.1.16 and 2.1.17 golden rows are NOT RUN**, for round one's reason unchanged, and `make test` observed TWICE: bare it dies at TinyGo (`requires go version 1.19 through 1.26, got go1.27`) and under `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6` it reaches the engine gate and refuses with `the built mod targets Factorio 2.1 and the binary is 2.0.` **The client run is NOT REACHABLE, still owed, and one question larger**: whether a client's renderer treats a chunk boundary as anything at all. It should not, and nothing here has hovered one, which is the one thing a reader should not take from this leg's green rows.
